'''Geoffrey Ernest Stedman''' (1 April 1943 – 3 May 2026) was a New Zealand physicist, with research interests including the foundations of [[Theory of relativity|relativity]], [[symmetry in quantum mechanics]], and [[ring laser]]s.<ref name="Ringlaser">{{cite web|url=http://www.ringlaser.org.nz/content/e_prof_geoff_stedman.php |title=E. Prof. Geoff Stedman |access-date=16 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130123002212/http://www.ringlaser.org.nz/content/e_prof_geoff_stedman.php |archive-date=23 January 2013 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born in [[Christchurch]] on 1 April 1943, Stedman was the son of Silas and Eleanor Stedman.<ref name="Whos who 2001">{{cite journal |editor-last=Taylor |editor-first=Alister |editor-link=Alister Taylor |title=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa 2001 |journal=New Zealand Who's Who, Aotearoa |year=2001 |publisher=Alister Taylor Publishers |location=Auckland |issn=1172-9813 |page=829}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19821026.2.155.4 |title=Deaths |work=[[The Press]] |date=26 October 1982 |page=39 |access-date=9 May 2026 |via=[[Papers Past]]}}</ref> He was educated at [[Christchurch West High School]], and studied at the [[University of Canterbury]], graduating with a BSc(Hons) degree in physics in 1965.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19601210.2.199 |title=Christchurch West H.S. |work=[[The Press]] |volume=99 |issue=29384 |date=10 December 1960 |page=15 |access-date=9 May 2026 |via=[[Papers Past]]}}</ref> He subsequently undertook doctoral studies at [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College, University of London]], where he earned his PhD under Douglas Newman in 1969.<ref name="Ringlaser"/><ref name="Chronicle 2003"/>

In 1969, Stedman married Rachel Ann Dodd in [[Barnstaple]], Devon, and the couple went on to have one child.<ref name="Whos who 2001"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ancestry.com.au/search/collections/8753/records/38000196 |title=Geoffrey E Stedman in the England & Wales, Civil Registration Marriage Index, 1916–2005 |publisher=Ancestry.com Operations |access-date=9 May 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Career ==
After post-doctoral research at Queen Mary, Stedman returned to lecture at the University of Canterbury in 1971.<ref name="NZine">{{cite web |url=http://www.nzine.co.nz/features/geoff_stedman.html |title=Professor Stedman recipient of 2001 Research Medal |date=1 March 2002 |first=Bob |last=Kirk |access-date=16 October 2014 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> During his career, he focused on a range of research areas, but he was particularly interested in ring lasers from the 1980s onward. In collaboration with the [[Technical University of Munich]], Stedman and his team built a series of ring lasers in the [[Cashmere Caverns]]. The lasers, regarded as some of the most sensitive and advanced in the world, were able to detect earthquakes around the world, and were also used to investigate variations in the earth's rotation.<ref name="Chronicle 2003"/>

Stedman taught undergraduate papers across physics, from applied physics to theoretical and mathematical physics.<ref name="Chronicle 2003"/> He was instrumental in the introduction of physics papers aimed at arts students.<ref name="Chronicle 2003"/> Of his career, Stedman said at his retirement: <blockquote>"It was absolutely a thrill to help and educate young people and be involved in their decisions. It's been a very great privilege."<ref name="Chronicle 2003"/></blockquote>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1989,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/s-u/ |title=The Academy: S–U |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=16 October 2014}}</ref> and in 1994 he won the society's [[Hector Medal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |title=Hector Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=16 October 2014}}</ref> He was awarded the Canterbury Research Medal in 2001.<ref name="NZine"/> 

Stedman retired in 2003, having published over 160 scientific papers, and was granted the title of emeritus professor.<ref name="Chronicle 2003">{{cite journal |last=Hartley |first=Lynette |date=28 August 2003 |title=Teaching a 'privilege' – retiring physics professor |url=https://digitalvoyages.canterbury.ac.nz/omeka-s/files//original/22aeea5d0e3ca0c9f7d6f0363f0d6c52a82096c1.pdf |journal=Chronicle |publisher=University of Canterbury |volume=38 |issue=13 |page=2 |access-date=9 May 2026}}</ref>

==Later life==
In retirement, Stedman lived in Christchurch, and continued to work part-time at the university.<ref name="Chronicle 2003"/> He died at a care home in the suburb of [[Sydenham, New Zealand|Sydenham]], on 3 May 2026, at the age of 83.<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news |url=https://www.legacy.com/nz/obituaries/the-press-nz/name/geoffrey-stedman-obituary?id=61427932 |title=Geoffrey Stedman obituary |date=9 May 2026 |work=[[The Press]] |access-date=9 May 2026}}</ref>
